## Introduction
One of the most popular professional sports in Canada and the United states is Ice Hockey. Hockey brings excitment and goal scoring to the ice. In every game there are a handfull of goals that determine who wins the game. In this study we look at what factors contribute to total goals scored by a team in a game. Some of the factors that we will be looking at include power play opprotunities, shots on goal, shots blocked, home or away, and others. By looking at what factors are associated with more goals being it scored it will help teams to know what they need to focus on in order to score more goals. It also can help managers, fans, and even brodcasting networks know which games will have characteristics associated with more goals being scored. All of thsi data will help give more information and imporve the game adn entertainment vaule of hockey.   

## Research Questions
How do much do different factors in a game contribute to the amount of goals scored in an NHL game, leading to the higher scoring game?
How well can we predict how many goals are scored based off of a model to predict goals scored by a team in a game based off of the factors we studied?

## About Data
The data was collected by using Kevin Sidwar’s “documenting the still un-documented NHL stats API”. There was no licisnceing that was found on kaggle when the data was collected and all of the information on here is public knowledge and could be found if you took the time your self. I don’t think there is any privacy or ethical concerns with this dataset.
The data includes scores and measured statistics from NHL games over many years. Some of the measured statistics include the amount of goals scored, the amount of shots, which teams were home or away, the amount of power play opprotunities and many other commonly measured hockey statistics.
